newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Q3 housing starts rise 3.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Q3 housing starts rise 3.2 pct.

text.p: Canadian housing starts rose by 3.2 percent in the third quarter to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 128,600 units from a 124,600 units in the second quarter, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Thursday.
Actual housing starts fell to 37,190 in the third quarter from 38,435 the month before. The SAAR is a quarterly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said the new housing market kept a positive, though moderate, momentum in the third quarter.

"The resale market is stable, at high levels, and consumers continue to show restraint, but there are new lows on mortgage rates and great affordability. This should be sufficient to keep construction trends up," Gilles Proulx, chief economist at CMHC's market analysis center, said.
